english.title: Attempt to handle stolen goods
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) attempted to dishonestly undertake or assist in the retention, removal, disposal or realisation of stolen goods, namely **(..SPECIFY THE GOODS..),

(A)_[to the value of **(..SPECIFY THE AMOUNT..)]_
(B)_[of a value unknown]_

belonging to**(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..) by or for the benefit of **(..SPECIFY THE TERM - ANOTHER - OR SPECIFY THE NAME OF A CO-ACCUSED..) or attempted to dishonestly arrange so to do, knowing or believing the same to be stolen goods
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(1) of the Criminal Attempts Act 1981.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
attempt to dishonestly undertake/assist in the retention/removal/disposal/realisation of
stolen goods belonging to another by/for benefit of another or
attempted to dishonestly arrange to do so
knowing/believing them to be stolen goods

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Mandatory drug test required if 18 or over
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Special evidence (section 27(3) Theft Act 1968) may be introduced, at the trial of a person charged with this offence, in certain circumstances.
(ii) The term 'another', if used in this charge, must refer to someone who is NOT the defendant or one of the co-accused (R v Gingell 1999).

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Fourteen years imprisonment.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
